description: Where to go snorkelling in India, from Andaman reefs such as Elephant Beach, North Bay and Jolly Buoy to the lagoons of Lakshadweep and the Konkan and Karnataka coasts, with the best months, how guided snorkelling works and how to protect the reef.
dek: Snorkelling is the simplest way to see India's coral reefs: no course, no heavy equipment, and many sites are a short boat ride from the beach.

intro: Snorkelling means floating face-down on the surface with a mask, snorkel and usually a life jacket, looking at the reef below. In India most snorkelling is guided: a local guide swims with you, often holding a ring buoy for less confident swimmers, and points out corals, clownfish and turtles when they appear.

The best snorkelling in India is in the Andaman Islands and Lakshadweep, where the reefs are shallow and the water is clear in the dry season. There is also snorkelling off Malvan and Tarkarli in Maharashtra, at Netrani Island in Karnataka and around Grande Island in Goa, though visibility on the mainland coast is lower.
quickAnswer: The best places for snorkelling in India are Elephant Beach on Havelock Island, North Bay near Port Blair and Jolly Buoy Island in the Andamans, the lagoons of Lakshadweep, Neil Island, and Malvan, Netrani and Grande Island on the west coast. Go between about November and April for calm seas and clear water. Guides and life jackets are usually provided, so non-swimmers can join.
takeaways: The Andamans and Lakshadweep have India's best snorkelling reefs.
Most snorkelling is guided and includes a life jacket, so strong swimming is not essential.
The best months are roughly November to April; the monsoon brings rough seas.
Jolly Buoy is in a marine national park and is open only in season; boats leave from Wandoor.
Never stand on or touch coral, and use reef-safe sunscreen or a rash guard instead.

items.name: Elephant Beach, Havelock Island
body: Elephant Beach, reached by boat from Havelock's jetty or a forest walk, has a shallow reef close to the shore and is the most popular snorkelling spot in the Andamans. It is busy in the middle of the day; go early.

facts.Access: Boat or forest trek from Havelock

items.name: North Bay Island, Port Blair
body: North Bay, facing Port Blair, has coral in shallow water and is combined with glass-bottom boat rides, sea walks and try dives. It suits a half day from Port Blair.

image.alt: Coral in clear shallow water at North Bay Island, Andaman
image.caption: North Bay Island

items.name: Jolly Buoy Island, Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
body: Jolly Buoy lies in the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, about an hour by boat from Wandoor near Port Blair. It has some of the best-protected shallow reefs in the islands. Entry is by permit through the forest department, numbers are limited, plastic is banned, and the island is open only in the dry season (Red Skin Island is used when Jolly Buoy is closed).

items.name: Neil Island
body: On Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Bharatpur beach has calm, shallow water for snorkelling at high tide, and guides take snorkellers to nearby reefs.

sections.heading: Snorkelling in Lakshadweep
paras: Lakshadweep's islands are coral atolls with shallow lagoons protected by an outer reef. Snorkelling in the lagoons at islands open to visitors, such as Agatti, Bangaram and Kadmat, is calm and clear in the dry season, and resorts and tour packages usually include it.
Every visitor needs an entry permit, usually arranged with the tour package, and the islands are reached by flight to Agatti or by ship from Kochi.

items.name: Agatti Island
body: Agatti, with the islands' airstrip, has a lagoon with shallow coral and seagrass where turtles are often seen.

image.alt: Reef fish over coral in the lagoon at Agatti, Lakshadweep
image.caption: Agatti lagoon

items.name: Malvan and Tarkarli, Maharashtra
body: Boats from Malvan jetty take snorkellers to rocky reefs near Sindhudurg Fort. Visibility is best from about November to March. It is a short, inexpensive outing on a Konkan coast trip.

items.name: Netrani Island, Karnataka
body: Dive operators in Murudeshwar also take snorkellers to Netrani Island, about an hour offshore. The reef has more fish than most mainland sites.

items.name: Grande Island, Goa
body: Boat trips from south Goa to Grande Island often include snorkelling and dolphin spotting. Water clarity is modest but it is easy to add to a Goa holiday.

sections.heading: How guided snorkelling works
list: Guides provide a mask, snorkel, fins and a life jacket. Check that the mask seals on your face before getting in.
Non-swimmers can often hold a ring buoy while the guide tows them over the reef.
Breathe slowly through your mouth; if water gets in, lift your head and clear the snorkel.
Float flat and keep your fins away from the reef; standing up in shallow water damages coral.
Sessions last 20 to 45 minutes, which is enough for most beginners.

safety: Wear a life jacket if you are not a strong swimmer, and stay near your guide.
Watch the tide and current; snorkel only where local guides say it is safe.
Follow crocodile warnings in the Andamans and avoid creeks and mangrove mouths.
Protect yourself from the sun with a rash guard; the back of your legs burns quickly.
Do not touch coral, sea urchins or fish, and never feed fish.
Do not take coral, shells or sand; it is illegal in protected areas and harms the reef.
packing: Your own mask if you have one (a better fit than rentals)
A dry bag for phone and cash on boats

faqs.q: Where is the best snorkelling in India?
faqs.a: The Andaman Islands, especially Elephant Beach, North Bay and Jolly Buoy, and the lagoons of Lakshadweep.
Yes, at most guided sites. You wear a life jacket and the guide often tows you with a ring buoy.

faqs.q: What is the best time for snorkelling in the Andamans?
faqs.a: About November to April, when seas are calm and the water is clear.

faqs.q: Is snorkelling better than scuba diving?
faqs.a: They are different. Snorkelling is easy, cheap and shallow; scuba lets you go deeper and see more. Many people snorkel first and try a scuba dive later.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to snorkel at Jolly Buoy?
faqs.a: Yes. Jolly Buoy is in a marine national park, and entry permits are issued through the forest department, usually arranged with the boat ticket from Wandoor.
